storyboard: Angle: The most incredible part of the fastest 100m ever is that the runner was slowing down to celebrate. Shape: 6 segments. Reveal structure. Hook with the contradiction (slowing down), show the evidence (chest tap), reveal the number (9.58), show the dominance (the gap), contextualize the record (untouchable), and kick out on the implication (he could have been even faster). Rhythm is fast-fast-hold-fast-fast-hold. Three-channel plan: Seg 2, voice adds detail (celebrating) over footage of the chest tap. Seg 4, text/voice/footage all agree to emphasize the 2-metre gap. Seg 6, text/voice create tension against the celebratory footage by asking what the true limit was.
label: WORLD RECORD
structure: reveal: withhold the record time until segment 3, then build on its significance.
voice_script: In the final of the 2009 World Championships, the fastest man in history was already celebrating before he even crossed the line. The clock stopped at 9.58 seconds. He beat the field by two full metres—an unheard-of margin in elite sprinting. In all the years since, no other athlete has come within a tenth of a second of the time. So the untouchable world record was set by a man who wasn't even running flat out. Which leaves one question.
